conventions.rotation: hope_frame_utils.rotate_motion_to_hope_x(theta_deg=theta_total) applied ONCE to the ORIGINAL compiled artefact, about the frame-0 pelvis pivot (0.154225, -0.179537). theta_total = theta_pelvis + psi_aim. Pelvis yaw after is deliberately NOT zero -- zeroing it is the bug that made 4 of 5 motions unable to return a ball.
conventions.grip: --grip off (identity mount). The registry's 40.26 deg human grip does NOT apply to these robot-space canonical clips; the marker is the only authority.
conventions.control_point: mujoco site 'right_racket' via check_motion_target_alignment.racket_control_point_series; velocity = clean_point_velocity(+-2-frame centred FD), trainer parity.
conventions.boxes: pos = min/max of the control point over the returnable frames backing the anchor, dilated by the env half-widths (0.10, 0.20, 0.10) m and floored at z = 0.78 (table 0.76 + ball radius 0.02). vel = anchor velocity +- (0.5, 0.5, 0.4) m/s, with the env's strictly-forward gate applied to vel.x.
conventions.anchor_rule: joint optimum, not returnability argmax: a frame must satisfy ALL of {phase-scan returnable > 0.5 under the DEFAULT ball, forward dominance (vx > 0 and |vx| >= |vy|) on the trainer-parity control-point velocity, blade z >= 0.78, measured face sign == the sign the family demands} and is then ranked by ANCHOR-EXACT return rate (the clip's own velocity and face through the venue contact law, no cone, no box).

metric_glossary.phase_scan_returnable: gen_stage1_questions.py --phase-scan: fraction of sampled incoming balls for which SOME commanded velocity inside the 25 deg / cone_mag cone returns the ball. This is what a solved question bank searches -- solvability, not fidelity.
metric_glossary.anchor_exact_return_rate: the clip's OWN control-point velocity and face at the anchor, pushed through virtual_ball.predict_paddle_contact + coarse_landing over the venue incoming-ball distribution. This is fidelity: does the motion as recorded return the ball. The two numbers disagreeing by a lot means the bank will command something the reference motion does not do.
metric_glossary.commanded_box_return_rate: uniform sample of the commanded pos x vel box through the same law. Relevant only if a box sampler is used instead of a bank.

bh_block.anchor_rationale: f24 = the joint optimum INSIDE the build's declared contact window [22,27]. f11 (phase 0.208) scores higher anchor-exact (0.5366 vs 0.4502) but sits in the backswing, outside the build window, so it is rejected on semantic grounds: anchoring the strike in the backswing would set the hitting target against the imitation target.

s0_highpress.anchor_rationale: f10, NOT the survey's f20. Three independent measurements move it: (a) at f20 the clip's own motion returns the ball 0.0000 of the time and needs a 4.0x blade-speed scale to reach 0.66; (b) at f20 the DEFAULT-ball scan scores 0.083, below the 50% bar every other anchor clears -- f20 is only returnable under the marker's own steep-descending-ball override; (c) f10 scores 1.000 under the default ball AND the slow ball, anchor-exact 0.8051, and passes forward dominance (vx 1.112 >= |vy| 0.950), which f7/f8/f9 do not. The survey correctly rejected f7/f8 for forward dominance but then jumped to lobe B; moving two frames later inside lobe A fixes it without leaving the shared ball regime. CAVEAT: f10 is outside the build's nominal contact window [16,20]. That window is weaker evidence here than for the other clips -- s0's marker nominal_event is an air-swing construction, not an observed ball contact.
